To complete and retain admission as a student in Texas Tech High School, you must work with an academic advisor and be enrolled in a minimum of four Texas Tech K-12 courses (dual-credit and Credit By Exams excluded). Generally, you will complete a total of six to seven credits per year (12-14 courses) and must also pass five State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness End of Course exams to meet graduation requirements.

To graduate with a Texas Tech High School diploma, you will take at least your last year of high school credits (25%) from Texas Tech K-12. Exceptions will be considered by administration on a case-by-case basis but the last semester (2.5 credits) must be taken from Texas Tech K-12.

**Graduation Credit Requirements for Texas Tech K-12**

To graduate from the Texas Tech K-12 program, students following the Foundation Graduation Plan with Endorsement need to complete a total of 26 credits. These credits are distributed across various subjects as follows:

- **English:** 4 credits
- **Math:** 4 credits
- **Science:** 4 credits
- **Social Studies:** 3 credits
- **Foreign Language (a language other than English):** 2 credits
- **Fine Arts:** 1 credit
- **Physical Education:** 1 credit
- **Electives:** 7 credits

Additionally, students must pass five State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness End of Course exams to meet graduation requirements. For more detailed guidance, students should work with a Texas Tech K-12 academic advisor.

About Students with Disabilities

Online instruction presents different challenges than those in a traditional classroom. The curriculum is rigorous and is reading- and writing-intensive. Successful online students are able to take initiative and manage their own time.

To qualify, the student's Individual Education Plan (IEP) needs to indicate that the Texas Tech K-12 online program is the appropriate instructional setting for the student and is the student’s least restrictive environment.

The student’s admission, review, and dismissal (ARD) committee has the responsibility of determining whether or not an electronic (online) course/program will meet the needs of a student with a disability. The committee will also take into account the nature of the asynchronous program and what services can be implemented online. It is crucial to note that the program is fully online, providing only services that can be provided virtually as the school does not have a physical location. To earn a Physical Education credit through the Texas Tech K-12 program, students typically engage in activities that can be completed independently and documented. Here are some general steps and considerations:

Characteristics Related to Potential Giftedness

Step 7: The student demonstrates innovative use of common materials both in the classroom and beyond. Some students show exceptional ingenuity in using everyday materials in new ways of adapting or combining common materials to serve quite different purposes from those for which the materials were originally designed. This type of ingenuity is a good indicator of creativity and originality as well as problem-solving.

Step 8: There are numerous opportunities both in and out of the classroom to observe the range of topics or areas in which a student appears to have some knowledge. The breadth of information that a student has is usually a good indicator of the variety of his or her interests. It is also a good indicator of effective long-term memory and the store of information a student has, both of which are strongly related to problem-solving ability.

Step 9: Student’s depth of information in a particular area. Some students develop extensive knowledge about some particular area such as space, birds, art, or music. A student who has gained such extensive knowledge has probably done so on his or her own as a result of along-term interest. Like breadth of information, depth of information is a good indicator of effective long-term memory and storage of information, both related to problem-solving ability.

Step 10: Student’s collections of materials or hobbies. Exceptional children tend to have hobbies or make collections of materials that are quite different from those of typical children in their age or grade group. For example, a potentially gifted fourth grade boy may have a collection of photographs of spider webs, whereas other fourth grade boys collect pictures of baseball players. Sometimes the content of the collections may be the same, but the potentially gifted child organizes his or her collection in a more systematic or novel way than does the typical child. Parents are particularly good sources of information about these kinds of things.

Any green bell is turned on. Click a bell and choose “Notifications off” to stop that type of message.

Clicking the "Bell" you should receive a box with several options. Selecting "Notifications off" will prevent you from receiving the notifications.

Course Discussions (Canvas)

You will be allowed to view discussions that are taking place within a course.

Canvas — Grades (course grade book)

Grades will allow you to view your student's individual course grades as well as overall course progress. Please note that there may be several assignments that require the teacher to grade prior to being able to move forward in the course.

Canvas calendar — upcoming student events & due dates

The calendar will allow you to view any upcoming dates that your student has populated. This may also be a good place to let students know about setting a due date for the course if there are deadlines for the school awarding credit.

Canvas Recent History — View recent student activity

History will show any "Recent History" in the course.

Supplemental Program Information

Anyone looking to supplement their current school curriculum or home school curriculum can enroll in Texas Tech K-12.  Our Texas Tech K-12 Supplemental Program (opens in new tab) is designed to allow students in elementary, middle and high school that allows students to work at their own pace. We have students who must do their work at home for various reasons, such as travel "outside" of the U.S. for extended amounts of time, have health issues, are actors, entertainers, and athletes who cannot fit the traditional schooling into their schedule. We have school all year and do not keep a traditional academic schedule, so it is possible to move through our program faster than the typical semester-based programs.

This is a self-paced program where all the instructional content is provided. The courses tend to be reading and writing intensive. Online courses require self-discipline and excellent time-management skills. The courses are not virtual classrooms and do not require any interaction with any other students or instructors. Each course has lessons, which are like chapters, and a final exam. The final exam will be proctored online by an online proctoring service.

Canvas Help (Portal Help & Guides for Counselors)

The Help guide will allow you to view Texas Tech K-12 grade help guides as well as Canvas Help Articles.

How to turn off Canvas notifications (Account > Notifications)

In Canvas, click Account → Notifications.

Any green bell is turned on. Click a bell and choose “Notifications off” to stop that type of message.

Clicking the "Bell" you should receive a box with several options. Selecting "Notifications off" will prevent you from receiving the notifications.

Live Help

If you need help, click the shield in the upper right-hand corner of the Canvas page to activate Proctorio's Live Chat.

Supporting Schools to Help Students Thrive

Texas Tech K-12 offers flexible, year-round solutions designed to supplement your school district's curriculum and support students in reaching their goals.
